problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,u+v,\,uv⟩$ at the point where $u=1$ and $v=1.$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of the Tangent Plane to a Parametric Surface Given Some Parameter Values
examples.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \big\langle v^2, \: u-v, \: u^2 \big\rangle$ at the point where $u=2$ and $v=-1.$
examples.worked_solution:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2v,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=2$ and $v=-1{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(2,-1) & =⟨0,\,1,\,2(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,4⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(2,-1) & =⟨2(-1),\,-1,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(2,-1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(2,-1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ -2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,-8,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=2$ and $v=-1$ correspond to the point 

$$
\big( (-1)^2, \: 2-(-1), \: 2^2 \big) = (1, 3, 4),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨4,\,-8,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-3,\,z-4⟩ & =0 \\ 4\cdot (x-1)+(-8)\cdot (y-3)+2\cdot (z-4) & =0 \\ 4x-8y+2z+12 & =0 \\ 2x-4y+z+6 & =0 \\ 2x-4y+z & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,2{u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,v⟩$ at the point $(1,2,0).$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $(1,2,0)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}u+v=1 \\ 2{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}=2 \\ v=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=0.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,4u,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2v,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,0) & =⟨1,\,4(1),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,4,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,0) & =⟨1,\,2(0),\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point $(1,2,0)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,0)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,0) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,-1,\,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
